description: We are explorers of ideas, ready for the challenge! Our team believes open scientific data can become meaningful discoveries through creativity, technology, and collaboration. We aim to develop innovative solutions using AI, data visualization, and interactive tools to make complex knowledge more accessible and contribute to the future of space exploration.
summary:
FireFile is an interactive scientific platform developed for NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge, designed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, connected, and understandable.

Fire behaves differently in space, creating unique challenges for astronaut safety. Although NASA provides extensive scientific data on these phenomena, exploring relationships between different investigations can be complex and time-consuming.

To address this challenge, FireFile brings together NASA's scientific investigations in a unified platform featuring interactive research maps, thematic clusters, advanced search tools, scientific profiles, and traceable connections between studies.

By combining data visualization, scientific organization, and artificial intelligence capabilities, we aim to facilitate the discovery of meaningful relationships, the exploration of experimental evidence, and the interpretation of combustion research.

Our mission is to transform complex scientific data into accessible and connected knowledge, supporting research on fire prevention, detection, and suppression while contributing to safer and more sustainable future space missions.
details:
FireFile: Connecting Microgravity Combustion Research

The Problem

Fire behaves differently in microgravity because the absence of buoyancy-driven convection changes flame behavior, heat transfer, and smoke transport. These differences create important challenges for fire safety aboard spacecraft.

NASA has conducted decades of combustion research, making valuable scientific information available through its Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. However, these investigations are spread across different records, publications, and datasets, making it difficult to identify connections and compare findings.

Our Solution

FireFile is an interactive research platform designed to organize, connect, and explore NASA's microgravity combustion investigations.

Instead of presenting research as isolated documents, FireFile creates a visual network that allows users to explore scientific relationships and thematic clusters.

What We Developed

Our platform includes:

  • Interactive Research Map: A D3.js network connecting investigations, with zoom, navigation, filters, and thematic clustering.
  • Scientific Research Profiles: Detailed information about each investigation, including objectives, experimental conditions, materials, scientific references, and official NASA links.
  • Documented Research Connections: 20 unique investigation pairs supported by 33 documented relationship records.
  • Research Discovery: Search tools, thematic classification, similarity comparisons, and relevance rankings.
  • Scientific Traceability: A curated collection of 78 source records, allowing users to distinguish NASA information from FireFile's interpretations.

Scientific and Technical Approach

We began by exploring NASA's PSI database and identifying investigations relevant to spacecraft fire safety.

We then organized the information into structured scientific records, categorized the research by themes such as fire prevention, detection, suppression, and combustion fundamentals, and developed an interactive interface to make the connections easier to understand.

The application uses React, TypeScript, and D3.js, with an emphasis on scientific transparency, accessibility, and responsive visualization.

We also investigated semantic artificial intelligence as a way to identify similarities between scientific studies, comparing an experimental multilingual embedding approach against simpler retrieval methods.

Experimental Data Exploration

As an additional scientific demonstration, we developed a focused visualization using selected data from NASA's Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight (SAME-R).

This demonstration connects a NASA investigation to tabular observations, a scientific chart, and a traceable explanation, illustrating how FireFile can move beyond catalog exploration toward evidence-based data interpretation.

The demonstration covers a selected subset of observations and is not intended to represent the complete experiment.

Impact and Future Development

FireFile aims to make scientific knowledge easier to discover, compare, and understand.

By connecting existing NASA research, the platform can support further investigations into spacecraft fire prevention, smoke detection, and flame suppression.

Future development may expand experimental data coverage, strengthen semantic retrieval, and support evidence-grounded scientific questions.

Our vision is to make NASA's open scientific research more accessible while preserving the accuracy, limitations, and provenance of the original data.
